snippet.title: Paris Jackson Reveals Her Favorite Michael Jackson Songs ❤ #michaeljackson
snippet.description:
What were Paris Jackson’s favorite Michael Jackson songs growing up? 🎶❤️

In this rare interview, Paris shares intimate memories of growing up with her father, Michael Jackson.

Although she and her brother Prince didn’t realize just how famous their dad was, they spent their childhood dancing, prancing around and building pillow forts while listening to his iconic Off the Wall album.

Paris also reveals two of her favorite songs: “The Lost Children” and “Whatever Happens,” featuring Carlos Santana.

Paris rarely shares these kinds of personal memories today, making this interview a special glimpse into life behind the scenes with the King of Pop.

snippet.title: Paris Jackson Was Mesmerized by Her Father, #michaeljackson
snippet.description:
Paris Jackson remembers watching her father, Michael Jackson, perform when she was just six or seven years old. ❤️

While thousands of fans filled the concert venues, young Paris was focused on just one person: her dad. She recalls being mesmerized by his performances, running through the crowds with her brother Prince, and the frightening moment she lost hold of Michael’s hand before he grabbed her and rushed away.

For Paris, he wasn’t just the King of Pop. He was her father — and she was one of his biggest fans.

snippet.title: Prince Jackson Reveals His Thoughts on The Masks #michaeljackson
snippet.description:
For years, Prince Jackson didn’t fully understand why his father insisted that he and his siblings wear masks in public.

At first, he thought it was excessive. But as he got older, he began to understand what Michael Jackson was trying to do.

Prince explains how he realized he could walk around unnoticed when his father wasn’t with him, while crowds instantly formed whenever Michael appeared. It was then that he understood the masks weren’t about hiding—they were about giving his children something Michael could never have: privacy, freedom, and a normal childhood.

It’s a touching reflection on Michael Jackson’s devotion as a father and the lengths he went to protect his children.

📚 Get your copy of Remembering Michael: A Mother’s Story by Katherine Jackson using the link in the description.

🎥 Subscribe for more exclusive Michael Jackson interviews, rare archival footage, and untold stories.

⸻

Caption

snippet.title: When Thriller Broke MTV #michaeljackson
snippet.description:
Michael Jackson didn’t just create Thriller—he helped transform the entire music industry.

At a time when MTV was heavily criticized for a lack of Black artists in rotation, Michael Jackson shattered barriers and changed the way the world experienced music videos forever. Thriller wasn’t just a hit song or album—it became a cinematic event that redefined pop culture and elevated the music video into an art form.

As we reflect on Michael Jackson’s lasting impact, we remember one of his greatest achievements: using music, performance, and visual storytelling to transcend racial and cultural boundaries around the world.

In our documentary, Michael Jackson’s Genius Explained, hear directly from people who were part of Michael’s creative journey—including Travis Payne, Michael’s longtime choreographer, Tito Jackson, his brother, and Ron Alexenburg, the music executive who helped bring Michael to CBS Records, paving the way for the era that would eventually lead to Thriller.

Watch the full episode here and discover the genius behind the legend.

Pick up a copy of Katherine Jackson’s memoir, Remembering Michael: A Mother’s Story, for more intimate stories about Michael’s life and legacy.

Stay tuned for more exclusive Michael Jackson stories, rare interviews, and untold history.

snippet.title: Katherine Jackson Opens Up About Michael's Legacy
snippet.description:
this episode, Michael Jackson’s mother discusses Michael's desire to be charitable from everything to music and driving around disadvantaged neighbors handing out $100 bills to strangers. Mrs. Jackson reveals that she was unaware that her son was in the Guinness Book of World records for his charitable efforts, but expressed that she knew that her son was giving and this is what he thought about the most.

Get Your copy of Remembering Michael - only on Amazon:
https://www.amazon.com/Remembering-Michael-Mothers-Jacksons-Memoir/dp/B0F99DMH3C/ref=tmm_pap_swatch_0?_encoding=UTF8&dib_tag=se&dib=eyJ2IjoiMSJ9.w11_vmUeiJNJpSU1UkDklyWWaGaOBatxhmiIwmOCxb4.wWLcSmTNIR0DxeQ6WO9olmpsOjH53qdePXFowGfqyn4&qid=1773183702&sr=8-1

Katherine also shares what it was like having her son at home under the same roof, before he decided to move out to Neverland. She shares her journey of living at the family home in Havenhurst for 41 years. The family first moved to California when Michael was young and then he rebuilt their ranch style home into an English Tudor Estate, because that was mother's favorite style at the time.



And finally, Mrs Jackson, shares her shock and delight when Michael married Lisa Maris Presley and eventually moved on to marry Debbie Rowe.

snippet.title: Ten Must-See Performances That Changed Music Forever
snippet.description:
10 Iconic performaces in Music History!

Step into the rich tapestry of music history, where each note and beat tells a story of passion, rebellion, and sheer brilliance. We're about to embark on a journey through the live performances that have not only entertained but also defined entire generations.

10. Marilyn Monroe's 'Happy Birthday Performance
Kicking off our list at number ten is an iconic Hollywood moment etched in history – Marilyn Monroe's enchanting performance of 'Happy Birthday, Mr. President' for John F. Kennedy in 1962. The allure of Monroe's seductive rendition has left an indelible mark on pop culture. 

 9. Elvis Presley, the undoubted King of Rock and Roll, showcased his unparalleled stage prowess in the '68 Comeback Special, a defining moment in his illustrious career. Airing in 1968, this televised event marked Presley's return to live performances after years of focusing on movies. The special not only reaffirmed his musical brilliance but also reignited the raw, charismatic energy that made him a cultural phenomenon. 

8. Madonna's MTV Video Music Awards performance
Securing the eighth spot on our list is Madonna's groundbreaking 1984 MTV Video Music Awards performance, a pivotal moment in pop culture history. In 1983, Madonna's earlier MTV VMA performance of the same song had already sent shockwaves through the industry, pushing boundaries and etching her name in the annals of music history. 

7. Rolling Stones Altamont
 Securing the top spot is The Rolling Stones' 1969 performance at the Altamont Free Concert, featuring a provocative rendition of 'Sympathy for the Devil.' This landmark moment in rock history captured the essence of rebellion with the band's raw energy and the charged atmosphere of the event. 

6. Queen's Live Aid Performance
Securing the fifth position is Queen's iconic Live Aid performance, an electrifying spectacle that stands as a pinnacle in musical history. The 1985 Wembley Stadium show saw Freddie Mercury masterfully command the stage, captivating the massive audience with unparalleled charisma. In a performance that defined Queen's enduring legacy, Mercury had the entire stadium in the palm of his hand, creating a transcendent connection with the crowd. 

5. Zeppelin's Royal Albert Hall.
At the fourth spot on our countdown is Led Zeppelin's legendary 1970 performance at the Royal Albert Hall, featuring their electrifying rendition of "Stairway to Heaven." This performance is a testament to pure rock 'n' roll energy and musical mastery. Led Zeppelin, renowned for their dynamic stage presence, delivered an epic rendition that elevated the already iconic "Stairway to Heaven" to new heights. 

4. Jimi Hendrix's Woodstock Performance
At number 2 we have Jimi Hendrix's groundbreaking 1969 Woodstock performance, where he mesmerized the audience with an electrifying rendition of 'The Star-Spangled Banner.' Hendrix's unparalleled guitar mastery and unconventional interpretation of the national anthem made a powerful statement, solidifying his status as one of the greatest guitarists of all time. 

3. Prince's Super Bowl XLI
Taking the sixth spot is Prince's unforgettable halftime show performance at Super Bowl XLI in 2007, a moment that transcended entertainment and became a historic milestone in pop culture. The epitome of a Hollywood celebrity making musical history, Prince delivered an electrifying spectacle that showcased his virtuosity as a performer. Against a pouring rain, his iconic guitar solo during "Purple Rain" and dynamic stage presence mesmerized the audience, solidifying the performance as one of the greatest in Super Bowl history. 

2. Whitney Houston - National Anthem Super Bowl XXV
Securing number two is Houstan's unforgettable rendition of the SSB in 1991 - this performance showcased her range but sparked patriotism in the USA during the Gulf War. Her performance pulled 115M views in the US and 750 million viewers worldwise, it was so popular that it was released as a single shortly after. 

1. Michael Jackson's Motown 25
 Securing the seventh spot on our list is Michael Jackson's extraordinary performance at the Motown 25: Yesterday, Today, Forever special in 1983. This legendary moment in music history saw Jackson unveil the iconic moonwalk and deliver electrifying dance moves that transcended mere entertainment, showcasing his unparalleled talent. The performance not only captivated audiences but also marked a pivotal turning point in Jackson's career, solidifying his status as the King of Pop.

And there you have it.
Which performance do you think deserves the top spot? Let us know in the comments below - and don’t forget to subscribe 

Thank you for being a part of our community. Until next time, keep the music alive!

snippet.title: Blues Singer Bonnie Bramlett Shocks the staff of Roseanne #shorts #shockingmoment
snippet.description: After exploring gospel music in the 1980s, Bramlett married Danny Sheridan in 1988 and she changed her professional name to Bonnie Sheridan.[4] He became her manager and produced her next recordings. She fronted their group the Bandaloo Doctors,[4] with their self-proclaimed "revolutionary hard rockin' blues." The group's music attracted the admiration of many Hollywood celebrities. In 1990, Bonnie met Roseanne Barr at a rehab program fund-raiser, and she was soon cast as a semi-regular on the hit ABC series Roseanne.[2] Bonnie Bramlett (credited as Bonnie Sheridan) played a co-worker and friend (named Bonnie) of Roseanne Barr's character Roseanne Conner, with Danny Sheridan occasionally writing music and appearing as the character Hank the bass player.

snippet.description:
What Made Michael Jackson a Genius?

In this documentary, we explore the beliefs, values, and mindset that shaped one of the greatest artists in history. Through rare interviews and exclusive archival footage, discover how Michael Jackson's spirituality, relentless pursuit of perfection, and compassion for others influenced both his music and his life.

Featuring insights from Katherine Jackson, Tito Jackson, Prince Jackson, Paris Jackson, Bigi Jackson, Travis Payne, Ron Alexenberg, and Randall Sullivan, this documentary offers a rare look at the man behind the legend.

From the rise of Thriller and the creation of Neverland to Michael's commitment to healing the world through music, this film examines the ideas that inspired his work and the philosophy that guided his life.

If you've ever wondered what truly drove Michael Jackson's creativity, this documentary offers a perspective few have seen.
